Main run complete. Final answer: **K = 4 shared modes**, selected unanimously by BIC and leave-one-curve-out, passing all stability gates. Deliverables written: `analysis.py` (seeded, end-to-end, bit-for-bit reproducible — two consecutive runs give identical md5) and `results/modes.csv` (exact schema `tau,a_0..a_4`, header, curves ordered 0–4, rows sorted by descending tau).

## Recovered modes (amplitudes re-solved by NNLS at the final polished centres; independently re-verified to match the CSV within 5e-4 = the %.6g write-precision)
| tau (± from Jacobian SE on log10 tau) | phi ± SE | LOO tau drift (max) | a_0 | a_1 | a_2 | a_3 | a_4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38.82 (log10τ=1.589±0.019) | 0.879±0.018 | 0.053 dex | 1.002 | 0.892 | 1.047 | 0.935 | 1.394 |
| 1.068 (log10τ=0.029±0.024) | 0.921±0.041 | 0.022 dex | 0.743 | 0.822 | 0.954 | 0.946 | 0.965 |
| 0.03675 (log10τ=−1.435±0.039) | 0.875±0.065 | 0.021 dex | 0.710 | 0.801 | 0.787 | 1.017 | 0.972 |
| 0.00221 (log10τ=−2.656±0.041) | 0.829±0.030 | 0.032 dex | 1.109 | 1.208 | 1.194 | 1.335 | 0.970 |
Baselines a0 per curve: 0.050, 0.251, 0.299, 0.071, 0.108.

## K-vs-fit and K-vs-LOO table (n = 960 stacked complex points)
| K | SSR | rms | BIC | LOO_SSR | LOO_rms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|1|19.11|0.1411|−3677.5|50.63|0.2296|
|2|6.02|0.0792|−4738.9|43.15|0.2120|
|3|3.74|0.0624|−5147.2|41.18|0.2071|
|**4**|**3.10**|**0.0568**|**−5280.3**|**40.78**|**0.2061**|
|5|3.01|0.0560|−5261.0|40.83|0.2062|
|6|2.97|0.0556|−5223.6|40.84|0.2063|
BIC-best = LOO-best = 4 (no disagreement rule needed). K=5 gains only 3% SSR by splitting mode 0 into a collinear pair (log10τ 1.667/1.524, 0.14 dex apart) — rejected by both criteria.

## Methodology compliance (your points 1–7)
1. **Polished optimum reported**: during the first run I caught a real failure mode — scipy Powell with bounds returned points whose true projected SSR was worse than its start (5.92 vs 2.61 in a direct repro), because its bounded line search uses a surrogate. I patched `fit_K` to carry best-so-far explicitly and accept a Powell candidate only if its recomputed true SSR improves. The published fit is the polished one (SSR 3.097), and CSV amplitudes were re-solved by NNLS at those exact centres.
2. **Ordering**: tau-descending sort applied only when canonicalising solutions and writing the CSV; never a fitting constraint.
3. **Order rule**: BIC primary + LOO held-out check (above); agreement on K=4.
4. **Weighting**: equal weights; per-curve weighting considered and rejected on evidence — per-curve residual RMS is balanced: re {0.052, 0.050, 0.056, 0.061, 0.063}, im {0.049, 0.054, 0.061, 0.055, 0.066}.
5. **Structural questions stated explicitly**: (a) the log10 x ≈ +1.65/+2.7 pair = **two genuine modes** (log10τ = −1.435 and −2.656, i.e. loss peaks at log10 x ≈ +1.44/+2.66): both carry large summed amplitudes (4.29 and 5.81), sit 1.22 dex apart (far beyond the 0.05 merge rule), and survive restarts and every LOO refit; the "one very broad mode" alternative (K=3) is clearly rejected (BIC −5147 vs −5280; LOO 41.18 vs 40.78). (b) **a0 vs fastest-mode tail**: a0 = 0.05–0.30 reproduces high-x plateaus within ~0.02 once the fastest mode's residual tail (~0.1 at x_max) is included; caveat — curves 0 and 3 have a0 near the NNLS lower bound, so their a0 trades off mildly with that tail, and the mode at log10τ = −2.656 peaks only half a decade inside the right edge, making its τ the least well-determined of the four.
6. **Uncertainties** (stdout + `results/run_log.txt`, not extra CSV columns): per-mode Jacobian SEs above plus LOO-refit spread (std 0.012–0.026 dex). Restart stability: 31/67 multistart+polish candidates land within 1% of best SSR and **all 31 reproduce the same four centres to <0.1 dex (spread 0.000 dex)** — 4/4 modes pass the 80%/0.1-dex gate; φ spread ≤0.05 among them.
7. **Qualitative reproduction**: mean-curve re drop 3.897 (data) vs 3.914 (fit); fitted im ≤ 0.005 in 100% of points; per-curve low-x plateaus matched to ≤0.01 and high-x to ≤0.02; binned residual means (8 log-x bins × re and im × 5 curves) all within ±0.03 with no trend — most ≤ σ/√12 ≈ 0.015; the largest single bin (curve 3, lowest-x im bin, +0.050 ≈ 3σ_bin) is the only mild flag.

## Limitations
- Final rms 0.057 is ~14% above the second-difference noise estimate (0.05); consistent with noise, but a small unmodelled slow tail cannot be fully excluded.
- Jacobian SEs treat the NNLS active set as fixed (smooth-region approximation); no amplitude sits on the active boundary except the a0 remarks above.
- φ values quoted in my independent re-verification were rounded to 3 decimals; the 5e-4 amplitude agreement confirms no material discrepancy.
